newsitem.title: USA: Seagull Energy sets 17 pct spending rise.
newsitem.headline: Seagull Energy sets 17 pct spending rise.

text.p: Seagull Energy Corp said it has approved a capital expenditures budget for 1997 of $250 million, 17 percent higher than actual 1996 expenditures of $213.5 million.

Some $234 million of the 1997 budget is allocated to exploration and production, compared with $199.5 million in actual 1996 E&P spending. Practically all of the 1997 increase is targeted for projects outside North America.
Exploration spending is expected to reach nearly $85 million next year, compared with $77.5 million last year.
Some 35 to 40 percent of 1997 exploration dollars are expected to be spent outside North America, Seagull said.

Development spending in the new year is budgeted at about $139 million versus $108.2 million spent in 1996. Leasehold acquisitions are expected to total about $11 million in 1997, versus 1996 spending of $13.9 million.

The company said the capital expenditure total does not include some $37.5 million budgeted for small-scale acquisitions in its core domestic E&P areas during 1997, which compares with $29.1 million expended for such purchases last year.

In terms of wells, Seagull said, its plan anticipates 65 to 70 exploratory and about 220 development wells in 1997 versus comparable 1996 totals of 50 and 184, respectively. Nearly 30 of the 1997 wildcats are scheduled outside North America, versus only 11 such wells drilled in the prior year.
